chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwān, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, from his fathers, peace be upon them, from 'Ali, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his Family,
There is not in my nation any monks, nor travelers, nor silence, meaning silence.

key_terms.رَهْبَانِيَّةٌ: Monasticism or the state of being a monk
key_terms.سِيَّاحَةٌ: Traveling or journeying (often for spiritual or leisure purposes)

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet mean by 'rumm' (silence) in the context of his nation's characteristics?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his Family) distinguishes the Islamic Ummah from other traditions by rejecting monasticism (rahbāniyyah), wandering (sayyāḥah), and excessive silence (rumm). This triad highlights the Shia emphasis on active engagement in the world while maintaining spiritual purity, contrasting with ascetic withdrawal or passive quietude. The clarification of 'rumm' as silence underscores the value of balanced speech and presence rather than mere absence of noise.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Muhammed bin Hussain, from Abu’l-Jawza’, from Hussain bin ‘Alwan, from ‘Amru bin Khalid, from Zaid bin Ali, from his fathers, peace be upon them, from Ali, peace be upon him, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said:
There is not in my nation any monks, nor travelers, nor decaying. Meaning silent.
